unruled:f8962#1.evidence: i8962 p. 14, "If the correct applicable SLCSP premium is not the same for every month of 2025, check “No” and continue to lines 12 through 23." The f1095a.uniform question asks whether both columns are the same every month and says "Use the corrected column B if column B is blank, zero or wrong"; the monthly in_b_* questions ask for "the amount in column B, or the correct applicable SLCSP premium if column B is blank, zero or wrong (from the Marketplace's tool…)". A corrected column B that varies by month therefore makes uniform No, which is the line 10 route test. The completeness prompt does not include the foreign form's question text, only its refusals, which is why the reviewer could not see it.

unruled:f8962#2.evidence: i8962 pp. 4–5 and p. 16: if no APTC was paid, column B may be wrong, blank or zero, and the filer must determine the correct applicable SLCSP premium. The f1095a.mo_b question asks for "the monthly amount in Part III, column B (monthly SLCSP premium) … or the correct applicable SLCSP premium if column B is blank, zero or wrong (from the Marketplace's tool, for example HealthCare.gov/Tax-Tool)"; f8962.line11b sums f1095a.line33b, which is built from that answer.

unruled:f8962#3.evidence: i8962 p. 17 tells the filer to enter the correct applicable SLCSP premium in column (b) when the reported amount is missing or wrong, and the f1095a.in_b_<month> question does ask for "the amount in column B, or the correct applicable SLCSP premium if column B is blank, zero or wrong (from the Marketplace's tool…)". But the same question ends with "; zero if blank", which contradicts that instruction for a covered month whose column B is blank: a filer following the trailing clause enters zero and understates column (b) and the PTC. The first clause covers the source's rule; the trailing convention does not. BUG-0298 records the wording defect and T-165 schedules the fix at the next f1095a change.

unruled:f8962#5.evidence: Two limbs. A claimable filer is refused at the return level through sa.dependent (sa.standardraw → f1040.line12e; witness checked 2026-11-01). The estimate_100 question also now carries the intentional/reckless misreporting disqualifier (BUG-0296).

unruled:f1095a#1.evidence: The unpaid-premium and not-lawfully-present cases the claim names are refused by f8962.other, whose question asks whether "any part of a month's premium was not paid by the due date of your return … or a Form 1095-A shows zero in column A for a month whose premium you paid" and whether "someone enrolled … was not lawfully present"; answering yes refuses the return (i8962 p. 4 and p. 6, cited by the gate). The tool does not compute the adjusted column A in those cases; it refuses them, which is what the completeness rule asks for.

unruled:f1095a#2.evidence: The same f8962.other refusal covers the unpaid-premium cases under i8962 p. 16 Column (a) and p. 17 Column (b), including the instruction to enter -0- in column (b) when the month's premiums were unpaid and to enter the SLCSP when they were paid by the due date; the not-lawfully-present limb is named in the same question. Those returns are refused, not computed with the unadjusted column B.

unruled:f1095a#3.evidence: i8962 p. 15's December-marriage addition applies to a 2025 marriage with separate plans. A joint return with a 2025 marriage and Marketplace coverage before the first full month of marriage is refused by f8962.marriage (i8962 p. 13, Table 4). A married filer using head-of-household status under the considered-unmarried rule has a tax family that excludes the spouse, so the p. 15 addition, which requires the spouses' separate plans to be in the two tax families, does not apply; the b_counted answer therefore cannot reach a computed return in the December-marriage case. This corrects the earlier evidence's reliance on household.filing_status_conflict, which tests only single+married and joint+not-married.

unruled:f1095a#4.evidence: A policy shared with another tax family is refused by f8962.alloc (i8962 p. 12, Allocating policy amounts: the policy covered someone in the tax family and someone in another tax family, or a divorce or separation in 2025 with a shared policy), which refuses lines 24 and 25.
